what_its_for: Alprazolam is used to treat anxiety disorders and panic disorder. It helps calm your nervous system to reduce feelings of worry, fear, and tension. It belongs to a group of medicines called benzodiazepines.
how_to_take: Take alprazolam exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the regular tablet whole with a full glass of water. You may take it with or without food. If you have the extended-release tablet (Xanax XR), swallow it whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. If you have the orally disintegrating tablet (Niravam), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve, then swallow. Do not take more than your prescribed dose, and do not take it more often or for longer than directed.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how you respond. For anxiety, the typical starting dose is 0.25 mg to 0.5 mg taken 3 times a day. For panic disorder, doses may be higher. Never change your dose on your own. Always follow your doctor's instructions. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms such as seizures, shaking, and severe anxiety.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within an hour or two of your scheduled time. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store alprazolam at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in a safe, locked place out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused medicine safely — do not flush it down the toilet unless the label says so. Ask your pharmacist about local drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking alprazolam. Alcohol can dangerously increase the sedative effects and may cause serious breathing problems, coma, or death. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Do not take other medicines that make you sleepy (such as opioid pain relievers, sleep aids, muscle relaxers, or other anxiety medicines) without first checking with your doctor. Avoid grapefruit juice, as it may increase the amount of alprazolam in your blood.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: difficulty breathing or very slow breathing, extreme drowsiness or confusion, thoughts of harming yourself, mood changes such as depression, aggression, or hallucinations, seizures, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), or severe allergic reactions such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also tell your doctor if you feel the medicine is no longer working, if you notice signs of dependence or feel you need more of the medication, or if you want to stop taking it.
when_it_works: Alprazolam works fairly quickly. You may start to feel calmer and less anxious within 15 to 30 minutes of taking a dose. The effects usually last about 4 to 6 hours for the regular tablet. The extended-release tablet works more gradually and provides longer-lasting effects. Keep in mind that this medicine treats your symptoms but is not a cure. It is typically meant for short-term use.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): You may be more sensitive to the effects of alprazolam, including dizziness and confusion, which can increase the risk of falls. Your doctor will likely prescribe a lower dose. Pregnancy: Do not use alprazolam during pregnancy unless your doctor says it is absolutely necessary. It can harm an unborn baby and may cause withdrawal symptoms in newborns. Breastfeeding: Alprazolam passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: This medication is generally not recommended for use in children under 18 years old. Liver or kidney problems: Your body may process this medicine more slowly. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose.
